summary: This RFC specifies how clients get notified about changes in a centralized conference (XCON). It reuses the SIP event package for conference state and adds support for the XCON data model and for partial notifications that report only what changed.

plainLanguage.summary: When something changes in a meeting, people who care get a short message. This sets out how that message is sent, including small messages that only say what is new instead of repeating everything.

questions: sip conference event package xcon extension
what is the xcon conference event package
what is a partial notification in sip conferencing
subtitle: How a centralized conference server tells clients what changed, either by resending everything or by sending only the differences.

tldr.problem: The XCON framework needs a notification protocol that reports conference state to clients, but sending the whole conference state for every small change wastes bandwidth.
tldr.mechanism: It reuses the SIP event package for conference state and adds two XML formats: a full-state document using the XCON data model, and a diff document that lists added, removed and replaced pieces.
tldr.outcome: Clients and servers can choose full or partial notifications through the Accept header, and legacy clients keep working because servers must also support the older format.

today: RFC 6502 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 4575 and the XCON data model in RFC 6501.

sections.title: Notifications in Centralized Conferencing
sections.content:
The XCON (Centralized Conferencing) framework in RFC 5239 defines a notification service. It gives authorized parties updates about the state of a conference instance, using a notification protocol between a notification client and the conference's notification service.

This document specifies how to use the SIP (Session Initiation Protocol, RFC 3261) event package for conference state, defined in RFC 4575, as that notification protocol. RFC 4575 also defines a data format for the package. The XCON data model in RFC 6501 extends that format with new elements and attributes, for example for floor control.

The notification protocol here carries everything in the XCON data model, which is the data from RFC 4575 plus the RFC 6501 extensions. It adds a partial notification mechanism based on XML patch operations from RFC 5261.
sections.plainLanguage: A meeting room has a board that shows who is in the meeting. This RFC says how the board keeps everyone's copy up to date.

sections.title: Three Notification Formats
sections.content:
A client gets notifications by subscribing to the conference event package at the server, as RFC 4575 specifies. The NOTIFY requests in that package can carry an XML document in one of three formats:

  • application/conference-info+xml, the original format from RFC 4575.
  • application/xcon-conference-info+xml, which gives the user agent the whole state of a conference instance.
  • application/xcon-conference-info-diff+xml, which gives the user agent the changes since the last notification sent to it.

The last two are new in this specification.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three kinds of notes: an old-style full note, a new-style full note, and a short note that says only what changed.

sections.title: Full Notifications and Backwards Compatibility
sections.content:
A subscriber signals support for full notifications by listing application/xcon-conference-info+xml in the Accept header field of its SUBSCRIBE requests. The server then has the option of returning documents in the XML format of RFC 6501, carried in bodies of that type.

Compatibility rules protect older software:

  • A server that supports the xcon-conference-info+xml type MUST also support application/conference-info+xml, so legacy clients can still read notifications.
  • A client that supports the new type SHOULD also support the old one, so it can talk to legacy servers.
sections.plainLanguage: A new phone should still be able to talk to an old phone. So new servers must still speak the old language, and new clients should too.

sections.title: Partial Notifications: Generating and Applying
sections.content:
With the full format, any change to one element makes the server send the whole conference state. That does not meet the efficiency needs of some bandwidth-constrained environments. Partial notifications report changes more efficiently. Servers that follow this RFC MUST NOT use the older <state>-based partial mechanism of the SIP event package, and MUST use this one instead.

A subscriber signals support by listing application/xcon-conference-info-diff+xml in its Accept header. On the server side:

  • The first notification after a subscription is installed MUST carry full state, with Content-Type application/xcon-conference-info+xml.
  • A partial notification uses the diff content type and SHOULD include only what changed. What counts as a change is up to the server's local policy.
  • Additions go in <add> elements, removals in <remove> and changes in <replace>.
  • The server MUST NOT send a new partial NOTIFY until it has a final response to the previous one or that request has timed out.
  • On a SUBSCRIBE refresh or termination, it SHOULD send the full document.
  • If it switches to partial notifications from another content type, it MUST send full state first.

The subscriber stores the first full document as its local copy. A later full document replaces that copy, and a diff document is applied to it. If processing a diff fails, the subscriber SHOULD renew its subscription, and it can fall back to normal operation by leaving the diff type out of its new SUBSCRIBE. If the server changes the content type mid-subscription, the subscriber MUST discard everything received so far and process the new content as that type requires.
sections.plainLanguage: First you get the whole picture. After that you only get sticky notes saying what to add, remove or swap. If a note makes no sense, you ask for a fresh full picture.

sections.title: The Diff Document Format
sections.content:
A diff document is an XML document that MUST be well-formed and SHOULD be valid. Its root element is <conference-info-diff>, in the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:xcon-conference-info defined in RFC 6501.

The root has one mandatory attribute, entity, whose value is the conference object identifier (XCON-URI) of the conference being described. Its content is an unordered sequence of <add>, <replace> and <remove> elements, followed by elements from other namespaces for extensibility. Clients MUST ignore unknown extension elements. The three operation elements may carry extension attributes beyond those in the base types of RFC 5261.

The RFC gives an XML schema for the format and an example. The example adds an entry to the allowed users list of conference conference123@example.com and replaces the user count with 5.
sections.plainLanguage: The change note has a title saying which meeting it is about, then a list of small instructions: add this, remove that, replace this.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The RFC lists four IANA actions: registrations for the MIME types application/xcon-conference-info+xml and application/xcon-conference-info-diff+xml, a URN sub-namespace registration for xcon-conference-info-diff, and an XML schema registration. Both MIME types use the same optional parameters and encoding considerations as application/xml in RFC 3023, and the IETF is the change controller.
sections.plainLanguage: The new kinds of note get official names in a public list, so nobody else uses the same names for something different.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says that encoding notifications in a different format does not have security implications. Implementers still need to follow the security considerations of the event package in Section 8 of RFC 4575, whatever format they use for notifications.
sections.plainLanguage: Changing the shape of the note does not change how careful you have to be. The old safety rules still apply.

items.title: conference-info+xml
items.text: The original RFC 4575 format, kept for legacy clients.

items.title: xcon-conference-info+xml
items.text: The whole state of a conference, using the XCON data model.

items.title: xcon-conference-info-diff+xml
items.text: Only the changes since the last notification.

viz.caption: PARTIAL NOTIFICATION FLOW (ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT FROM THE RFC)

messages.label: SUBSCRIBE
messages.note: Accept lists the full and diff content types.

messages.label: NOTIFY (full state)
messages.note: First notification must be the full document.

messages.label: final response
messages.note: Server waits for it before the next partial NOTIFY.

messages.label: NOTIFY (diff)
messages.note: Only add, remove and replace operations.

data.title: Partial update
data.code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<conference-info-diff
 xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:xcon-conference-info"
 entity="conference123@example.com">
 <add
  sel="*/users/allowed-users-list">  <target
  uri="sip:john@example.com" method="refer"/>
  </add>

 <replace sel="*/conference-state/user-count/text()">5</replace>

</conference-info-diff>
